this work shows that it is possible for the production of eurkaryotic proteins in prokaryotic cells.

the production of proteins that require disulfide bonds for their folding is possible in the cytoplasp of E. coli, and that the use of an exogenous sulfhydryl oxidas and disulfide isomerases can aid this process.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown the feasibility of using E.coli as a host to produce disulfide bond-containing proteins in the cytosol.
the production of disulfides in E. coli is a complex process, and that it requires the presence of a disulfide catalyst, a disulfide oxidase and a chaperone to achieve high yields.
the expression of eukaryote proteins with disulfide bonds can be achieved in E. coli, and that this is a very promising approach for the production of such proteins.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the production of disulfides in the cytoplastic of E.coli is possible and that the use of Erv1 is critical.
the expression of disulfide bond forming enzymes in the bacterial cytoplasm is an effective means to produce disulfide bond proteins in the cytosol.
the expression of eukaryotes proteins containing multiple disulfide bond in the cytoplams of E. coli can be improved by pre-expressing a sulfhydrydyl oxidase and a diulfide isomeras.
